title: Crypto investment amid fall: As Bitcoin hovers near $60K levels, experts answer if investors can expect recovery | Stock Market News
text:
Bitcoin price today: The world's largest cryptocurrency crashed near two-year lows on Friday, slipping below the $60,000 level before slightly recovering on Monday, 23 November, data showed. Cryptocurrencies have taken a beating as investors shifted risk-on investments toward recent IPOs in the artificial intelligence (AI) space, amid rising borrowing costs and regulatory changes anticipated following the Democratic win in the US mid-term elections, as per a Reuters report. Prateek Gupta, Head of Business at Mudrex, noted that historically, such sharp drops have been followed by 15-40% rebounds within weeks. “Markets now await US PCE inflation data on Wednesday. Support now stands at $56,700, while $61,700 acts as a major resistance,” he added. According to Riya Sehgal, Research Analyst at Delta Exchange, the crypto markets are witnessing a modest recovery after last week’s sharp sell-off, although the broader trend remains bearish. The overall crypto market capitalisation has risen by 2.4% to $2.1 trillion with 24-hour trading volume at $58.8 billion, according to CoinMarketCap. The Fear and Greed Index remained in the ‘Extreme Fear’ range but moved to 9, it added. Among the tokens, Bitcoin slipped 1.22% but retained dominance, holding 58.9% of the crypto market pie, followed by the second-largest crypto, Ethereum, which comprises 10% of the market, down a slight 0.67%; while the remaining tokens make up 31% of the crypto space, up 1.9%, CoinMarketCap data showed. Sehgal added that institutional sentiment remains cautious amid continued Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF outflows. She said, “Technically, Bitcoin faces immediate resistance at $60,600–$61,200, followed by $62,900, while $58,000–$59,000 remains an important support zone.” Nischal Shetty, Founder of WazirX, added, “Immediate support lies at $60,500-$61,000, followed by $59,400-$60,000. Resistance sits at $62,500-$63,300. Holding support could help consolidate the rebound, while reclaiming resistance would improve momentum.” She added that Ethereum faces resistance at $1,720–$1,730 and $1,770, with support around $1,600–$1,650. For the second largest token, Shetty feels that support sits at $1,680-$1,700, followed by $1,650-$1,665, while resistance lies at $1,750-$1,780. “Both assets recovering despite these withdrawals shows that ETF activity is only one market influence. Spot demand, derivatives positioning, liquidations and macro conditions can offset institutional flows before their effect becomes visible in prices,” Shetty added. According to the CoinSwitch Markets Desk, a sustained recovery will likely depend on improving technology equity sentiment, stabilising broader financial markets, and fresh institutional inflows over the coming sessions. Purvang Mashru, Lead Analyst at BitDelta India, concurred, “Our reading is that stronger aggregate volume needs broader participation before it supports a more durable recovery case. Trading can include selling, arbitrage and repeated transactions. Bitcoin support is near its observed daily low of $58,656, with resistance around $61,546. Holding gains while turnover broadens across chains would strengthen evidence of buyers absorbing sales. A return towards the low alongside fading activity would weaken it.” “Looking ahead, investors will monitor US equity-market performance, upcoming inflation data, ETF flows and Fed expectations. Until Bitcoin decisively reclaims $62,900 and Ethereum sustains above $1,770, the recovery may remain a relief rally rather than a confirmed bullish reversal,” Sehgal noted.
